evidence.note: Opening menu is a real decision - five distinct intents (Grapple control, Set up position, two Safe offense options at 53%/58%, Reset / recover) with different risk profiles.

The tie-up loop is punished immediately: 'The repeated tie-up stalls out - Hall gains escape momentum.' with Hall's momentum going 0 -> 1, followed at turn 4 by 'Hall uses the stale tie-up to reset with momentum.'

The warning does not stop the loop - collar_elbow is chosen on turns 1, 3, 5, 13 and 15 (5 of 11 player turns, move_repetition_rate 0.45) and the loop only ends because Hall knocks the player down, not because the player reacted to the feedback.
The one attempt at a counter-play fails and is punished: 'Hall reverses the pull off the top rope - only 1 damage, and turns the tables!', which sets up the 20-damage diving crossbody at turn 18.

No comeback window exists in the back half. Turns 9, 11, 19 and 21 are all 'Fight to your feet' with exactly one option, and the player's health falls 132 -> 53 while Hall only ever loses 1 HP (a reversal at turn 17).
Anticlimactic finish - the first cover of the entire match ends it 1-2-3 with near_fall_count 0 and no kickout tension.
Every option carries an intent label, a probability or 'auto', and a plain-language note ('steady damage and momentum without overcommitting'), so a new player can read the trade-offs without docs.

The anti-loop feedback is legible: the choice note changes from 'repeat loops lose steam' to 'tie-up is going stale - pay it off or reset before they steal momentum', and the resulting log names the consequence directly.

Status changes are explained rather than implied: 'Hitman is GROGGY - power moves and finishers are live!' and the very next menu (turn 7) narrows to two Reset / recover options noted 'clear the haze before they punish you'.

Groggy is presented as a modifier, not a position: the log reports GROUNDED plus 'Hitman is rattled - when they're forced up, big payoffs may open.', and turn 9 pays it off with 'Hitman rises - still groggy from the impact!'

Friction: 4 of 11 player turns (9, 11, 19, 21) present a single option, so the game asks for a decision where none exists. The note does explain the stake ('stand before they cover you; misses build escape momentum').
Minor ambiguity: 'Hall turns the tables!' is a bare reversal line that does not name the move reversed, unlike the fuller reversal text at turn 17.

stickiness.rematch_reason: The match is short, clean and legible, and the loop warning at turn 3 plants an obvious 'what if I had listened' hook. But it is a shutout - the player never lands a single offensive move, never sees a Finish option, and the last six turns are a scripted beating - so the pull is curiosity about the systems rather than desire to replay this matchup.
stickiness.next_experiment: Re-run seed 224 with a policy that switches off collar_elbow the moment the note reads 'tie-up is going stale' (turn 3) and takes the 58% Straight right instead, to see whether the player can build enough momentum to reach a Finish window before the Razor's Edge at turn 8.

evidence.note: Hook for a replay: the game explicitly told the player the loop was failing ('tie-up is going stale - pay it off or reset before they steal momentum') and the run continued anyway, so the alternate line is untested and interesting.
Unseen content teases a rematch: 'Hall snaps off razor's edge' and the FINISHER tag show a finisher/cover system the player never got to use from their own side.
Deterrent to replaying this exact configuration: the last six turns are 'Fight to your feet' into another CPU move, with the player at 53 HP and Hall at 131, offering no discovery.
The match ends on the first cover with near_fall_count 0, so the session closes without the drama beat that would drive an immediate rematch.
State shift is announced with weight: 'Hall snaps off straight right - Hitman takes 7 damage.' followed by 'Hitman is GROGGY - power moves and finishers are live!'
Finisher beat lands with three stacked lines - 20 damage, 'Hitman is rattled', and '- FINISHER - the next cover packs extra heat.' - and the promise is honoured at turn 22 with '+12 on the cover!'

Failed get-ups still produce feedback rather than a flat miss: 'still down and vulnerable, but the crowd is pulling them up.' plus 'Escape momentum builds for Hitman.' with momentum ticking 0 -> 1 -> 2.

Finish sequence has proper pacing metadata (1.0s after 'Referee: 1...', 1.5s after 'Referee: 2...'), but it is the only cover of the match and there is no near fall anywhere, so the payoff arrives without buildup.
The player side generates almost no payoff feedback: across 11 player turns not one landed offensive hit, so all the juice belongs to the CPU.

top_issues.summary: Total shutout with no comeback window. Across 22 turns the player lands zero offensive hits and Hall's health moves only 132 -> 131 (one reversal at turn 17), while the player falls 132 -> 53. Once the Razor's Edge lands at turn 8 the outcome is never in question.

The loop tax warns but does not break the loop. The stale-tie-up note appears at turns 3, 5 and 15 and the player still repeats collar_elbow on turns 1, 3, 5, 13 and 15; the loop ends only because the CPU knocks the player down at turn 8, not because the feedback changed behaviour.
4 of 11 player turns (9, 11, 19, 21) offer exactly one choice, 'Fight to your feet'. Prompting for input with a single option is friction rather than a decision.
near_fall_count is 0 and the match's only cover ends it immediately at turn 22, so the pin system's drama never activates.

Hall snaps off razor's edge - Hitman takes 20 damage.
Hall snaps off diving crossbody - Hitman takes 20 damage.
The finisher still echoes - +12 on the cover!
